limitations: Gemini independently reviewed exact bilingual event text, targeted run, located quotes and source metadata in a selective packet, not complete bytes of every website nor the original unpublished Commerce IIL/rescission letters. Producer checked all cited excerpts against retained extracted files.

Mayer Brown and Harvard Law Review are two independent legal analyses of the named June12 IIL. Neither establishes that the June30 lifting was independently analyzed as a general precedent; CNBC and Axios reporting of Anthropic’s announcement share that underlying actor origin.

The June30 company page includes a July1 update; the later status is used at the true October19 evidence cutoff, not backdated to June30. 5:21pm June12 is letter receipt, not proven exact completed service-shutdown timestamp.

A company-specific IIL is not necessarily a rule legally binding unrelated model developers. This is an editorial application of the L2-GOVERNANCE route subject to continued legal disagreement; downstream customers affected are not proof of cross-provider legal reach.
Actual production losses, users affected, AWS/Google/Microsoft cloud restoration, long-run sector trust and a causal GLM-5.2 acceleration were not established; no such effects enter impactIndex.
No human approval has been obtained. Any changed anchor event invalidates Arc dependency digests and requires new Arc review; this reviewer did not sign off on Arc publication.

identity.action: Commerce export restrictions on the two named Anthropic models lifted
identity.dateBasis: June12 company access statement for the named directive; June30 redeployment statement for named lifting, plus July1 updated access status as follow-up evidence. Node date remains original action date.
identity.deduplicationReason: Existing published node, same action and stage; correction not a new URL/event. Preserve original editorial.publishedAt and original slug.

classification.reason: The node identity is the company-specific government restriction or its lifting. Broad sector safety/business change is unobserved, so no separate secondary category claim.

significance.rationale: The dated named administrative access event and actual user-facing interruption/restoration are established; the general-application requirement of the governance milestone is not established for the one-company directive/lift. L1 correction is justified by affirmative scope analyses for June12 and named rescission for June30, not lack of discovery alone.
significance.whyNotHigher: Named removal and dated first-party restoration do not prove a general industry-wide rule or durable multi-case precedent. L2-GOVERNANCE requires all three conditions; this route is not satisfied. Legacy L2 scores are not grandfathered after substantive rewrite.
significance.whyNotLower: Named directive/lifting plus actual access-state change are directly documented and merit a historical node.

binding_or_precedential_action.rationale: Anthropic states Commerce lifted the named Fable and Mythos restrictions June30, restoring a changed administrative access status; original rescission letter not in packet.

applies_beyond_named_parties.rationale: The named Fable/Mythos lifting was announced; no retained legal instrument establishes a general lifting rule binding other model providers, and absence in this packet is not proof none existed.

independent_legal_analysis.rationale: Legal commentary retained concerns June12 named IIL and June26 exceptions, not independent legal analysis of the June30 rescission.

impactBasis.baseline: First-party Fable access had been suspended since the June12 directive and was not yet confirmed restored in the June30 announcement.
impactBasis.outcome: The July1 update says Fable first-party access returned under phased limits; external cloud completion not demonstrated; Mythos access confined to an approved set of US organizations.

consensus.reason: First-party access fact is recorded, but later market/regulatory consequences remain unestablished.

dispute.reason: No concrete separate dispute over whether the June30 named controls were lifted in scoped sources; uncertainty of legal precedent is a limitation, not a new litigated fact.
